items_missed: Never asked for or confirmed the move date — availability was never checked at any point in an 11-minute call
No agenda statement — opened with 'is now an okay time to chat about the details of your move' instead of laying out what the call would cover and how long it would take
Never asked whether they need packing services, despite the customer volunteering that loose items are in blankets and plastic bags and that they can't box everything
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked about access concerns at either address — parking, driveway, long walk from truck to door, HOA/gate restrictions (both homes are two-story houses in San Antonio subdivisions)
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Special-considerations probe was narrowed to heavy/delicate items only — no question about long walks, narrow hallways, or tight turns/stairwells
Walkthrough was never actually locked to a specific date and time — handed off to the support team with a vague 9AM–3PM Sat/Sun window and no confirmed slot
No confirmation email set up for this call — the only email mentioned was a post-walkthrough estimate email; no bolded recap, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the customer had to volunteer 'if they need anything else, just let me know'
Used the customer's name only once, in the opening line
top_strength: Excellent, honest resource-sizing judgment: he caught that a 2200 sqft home with only ~25 boxes doesn't match the standard two-truck/four-mover build and routed to a virtual walkthrough specifically so the customer wouldn't be over-resourced. He also refused to promise a weekend slot he couldn't guarantee, which built real trust.
coaching_note: The scheduling handoff undid the good work. Dustin sold the walkthrough well and the customer said yes twice, but the call ended with no date, no time, and no confirmation email — just 'someone will be in touch before 4:30.' On a walkthrough-scheduler call the booked appointment IS the close: pin a specific day and time window on the call (or warm-transfer to whoever can), then send a confirmation email with the time, the Zoom link, and a 'reply if that doesn't work.' Same call, tighten the front end too — he never once asked the move date, so he has no idea if this move is even in an available window.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and conversational — the 'I'm a big fan of those myself' moment on the storage tubs built real rapport, and 'I don't wanna make a promise I can't keep' landed as honest rather than deflecting; held back from a 5 only by heavy 'Okay. Gotcha.' repetition and using the customer's name just once.
